scope: Owner-directed Claude-to-Codex written handoff after review of the rig pilot's run-2 takes. The owner named take g1 the best wave draft and asked for its artifacts to be fixed, preferably by regenerating weak frames as LTX keyframes edited into the Aseprite animation through an after-completion self-audit (ODR-RIG-PILOT-G1-REPAIR-20261007). The owner also found the outfit art inconsistent and not sized to the sprite (ODR-OUTFIT-ART-REDRAW-20261007). The handoff documents how g1 was made (sources, guides, the exact ComfyUI recipe, the PC runner, take processing, outfits on clips, lessons). It gives a per-frame defect inventory with joints, mask boxes and hashes, and specifies the repair: a four-times-slower LTX keyframe retake of each weak span locked to g1's clean frames, ImageGen only for named keys and residual local repairs painted into the flattened frame, an eyes-only blink from owner-approved keys, frames 0 and 40 set to K0, and an Aseprite master. It specifies the self-audit checks, their calibration on g1 and the loop, plus per-view outfit art fitted by anchors with a three-view pilot, caps and gates. Claude also corrected its earlier g1 hand-frame count (about 11) to the verified inventory (17 frames, 5-12 and 25-33) in the pilot records, and added a pointer to the fashion brief. No image, runtime file or finding lifecycle changes. The outfit art has no active finding: the fashion runtime alpha already records its art as provisional pending owner review, and this review is recorded as an owner decision with the redraw specified.

lessons.lesson: In LTX-2.5 takes, hand smear tracks fingertip speed inside the 8-frame latent blocks: on g1 every smeared frame moves 10.7-15.1 cell px per frame and every crisp frame 4.4 or less. Keep generated fingertip speed under about 5 cell px per frame, for example by regenerating fast spans in slow motion and keeping every fourth frame.
A self-audit for hand quality must be calibrated on labelled frames before it can clear anything; simple colour and sharpness measures did not separate smeared from crisp hands on g1.

One garment drawing resized per cell cannot dress a multi-view character: it distorts proportions, loses detail below a pixel and puts the front of the dress on back views. Draw clothing per view and place it by anchors at one scale per view.
